assumptions: A meaningful set of Polish or CEE importers above the threshold experiences certificate exposure large enough to justify the stated pricing.
Forecasting can produce auditable decision value despite incomplete supplier emissions evidence.
Customs or trade-finance partners can refer customers without capturing most of the economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Paid diagnostics showing exposure or forecast improvements worth several times the fee, reliable outputs from actual customs and supplier data, conversion to annual subscriptions, quantified CAC and onboarding hours, and signed broker or adviser referrals.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Connecting emissions evidence to procurement and treasury decisions targets a measurable cash exposure rather than treating CBAM as a reporting-only task.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Certificate purchases create a direct, recurring financial consequence for covered importers, although achievable savings and customer data quality remain unproven.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: High contract values, annual prepayment, recurring price and shipment updates, and target 75-85% contribution margins are attractive; enterprise CAC, onboarding effort, specialist overhead, retention, and savings-based ROI need validation.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Mid-market importers with material exposure are a coherent high-value beachhead, but the 50-tonne threshold reduces volume and the Polish account count is unknown.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: A treasury-centered wedge differentiates from reporting tools, but customs, ERP, and ESG incumbents control adjacent data and relationships and can add forecasting.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: The decision layer can expand into supplier sourcing, scenario planning, working-capital management, evidence quality, other geographies, and adjacent trade costs.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Permissioned supplier benchmarks and embedded planning workflows could compound, but they do not exist yet and access remains customer-controlled.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Translating compliance inputs into cash forecasts and procurement scenarios can materially improve decisions if it demonstrably reduces exposure or forecast error.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: The definitive regime creates current certificate costs and repeated price updates, producing an immediate budget and forecasting trigger.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: Customs brokers and trade-finance advisers have well-aligned access to importers, but partnerships are unsigned and direct enterprise selling may strain a part-time founder.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A spreadsheet diagnostic permits capital-efficient validation, while supplier data, methodology liability, security, integrations, and enterprise sales add substantial execution risk.

highest_value_structural_change: Obtain a customs-broker channel partnership with permissioned data feeds so the product becomes the recurring treasury forecast attached to actual covered shipments.
main_structural_strength: The offer is tied to a current, quantifiable certificate cash cost and can demonstrate ROI through forecast accuracy or reduced exposure.
primary_score_limiter: The company controls neither importer nor supplier data, and repeatable enterprise distribution and defensible advantage over incumbent modules remain unproven.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: The threshold removes many small buyers, while large exposed importers may prefer existing customs, ERP, or ESG vendors with established data access.
